exercise1.hint: The empty case has to be handled before the division, not after it — len([]) is 0 and dividing by it raises.

exercise2.prompt: Summarising Numbers: The median, by hand

hiddenCases.name: negative and repeated values are retained
an even count averages the middle two
an empty list has no median
an outlier does not drag it
the caller's list is not sorted in place
the median is worked out, not imported

exercise2.hint: s = sorted(values) makes a sorted copy. With n = len(s) and mid = n // 2, an odd count gives s[mid]; an even count gives (s[mid - 1] + s[mid]) / 2.

questions.prompt: What does sum(scores) / len(scores) do when scores is empty?
questions.explain: len([]) is 0, and dividing by it raises. An empty column is common in real data, so this case has to be decided rather than discovered.

questions.prompt: Two classes both average 50. What does that tell you?
choices: Both had a top score of 50
questions.explain: Everyone scoring 50 and half scoring 0 with half scoring 100 give the same average. The spread is the part the average threw away.

questions.prompt: Reporting the smallest and ___ value next to an average shows the spread the average hides.
questions.explain: Two extra numbers turn a figure that can mislead into one that can be read.

questions.prompt: One score is mistyped as 900 instead of 90. Which summary barely changes?
questions.explain: The median depends only on the middle of the sorted values, so a single extreme value at the end hardly moves it.
